{{nihongo|'''Osake Shrine'''|大酒神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following five deities are enshrined. </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* {{ill|Qin (state)|Q34756|qid=Q34756}}{{ill|Qin Shi Huang|Q7192|qid=Q7192}}
:* {{ill|Yuzuki no Kimi|Q11066250|qid=Q11066250|lt=Yuzuki-kun}} (Yuzuki no Kimi)
:* {{ill|Sakenokimi Hata|Q54867522|qid=Q54867522}} (Hatanosake no Kimi)
; Aidenjin
:* Ehime no Mikoto - Kimono woman.
:* Otohime no Mikoto - Han weaver.

In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, there is one enshrined deity. In the same book, it is written as ``Osake Shrine {{sub| former name Daisojin}}, so it is known that the original name of the god was ``''Daisojin'''' {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine) | 1979}}.About the god of sake, "Koryuji Raiyuki" (Yamashiro Shukatsu Nogori Kaedeno Oigo-go Koryuji temple history, established in {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}}8 ({{ill|1499|Q6708|qid=Q6708}})<ref name="RAIYUKI">[{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} "Gunshoju Shinkyo Volume 18"] (Naigai Publishing, 1931-1937, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 384-388 frames. </ref> is said to be the ancestral god of {{ill|Qin Shi Huang|Q7192|qid=Q7192}} of {{ill|Qin (state)|Q34756|qid=Q34756}}, who came to Japan. It is said that a descendant of the Qin Shihuang (Q7192), a distant ancestor of the Qin clan (Q987290), proposed this shrine in 1979. The authenticity of the legend itself is not clear, but as the legend suggests, it is presumed to have been the guardian deity of the Hata clan, which developed the Uzumasa area from ancient times {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Shikiuchi-sha)|1979}}, and there is also a theory that links the god of sake with Hatanosake no Kimi, who appears in history books<ref name="Mizutani"/>. On the other hand, in {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}'s ``{{ill|Yongshufushi|Q18460389|qid=Q18460389}}'', the enshrined deity was {{ill|Mononobe no Moriya|fa|مونونوبه نو موریا|fr|Mononobe no Moriya|ja|物部守屋|nl|Mononobe no Moriya|pt|Mononobe no Moriya|ru|Мононобэ-но Мория|sh|Mononobe no Moriya|th|โมโนโนเบะ โนะ โมริยะ|uk|Мононобе но Морія|zh|物部守屋|zh_classical|物部守屋|qid=Q2424736}}, and one theory says that it was {{ill|Hata no Kawakatsu|fa|هاتا نو کاواکاتسو|fr|Hata no Kawakatsu|ja|秦河勝|zh|秦河勝|qid=Q5680877}}{{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Also, in "{{ill|Miyako meisho zue|ja|都名所図会|qid=Q11643495}}", the enshrined deities are {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}} Tenma Tenjin, and there are other theories that say it is Qin Shihuang and others that say it is Hata Kawakatsu {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.In addition to these, recent research has suggested that the original name of the god, ``大辟 (大辟),'' means the so-called {{ill|Dōsojin|de|Dōsojin|es|Dōsojin|fi|Dōsojin|fr|Dōsojin|hu|Dószodzsin|id|Dōsojin|it|Dōsojin|ja|道祖神|ko|도소진|mk|Сае но Ками|th|โดโซจิง|zh|道祖神|qid=Q269515}}, which ``avoids (keeps away) disasters.''{{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Gods)|1986}}<ref name="Mizutani"/>. In this theory, it is pointed out that {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} is written as stone in "Kuka Nikkoshu" and "Koryuji Engi" and that many stone deities are generally said to be {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahikokami}} (Dosojin) {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. === History ===

=== Founding ===
[[File:Kouryuji Roumon.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|{{ill|Kōryū-ji|de|Kōryū-ji|fa|معبد کوریو|fr|Kōryū-ji|ja|広隆寺|ko|고류지|my|ခိုးရူးဂျိ|zh|廣隆寺|qid=Q3076920}}}}]]
Regarding its founding, "Koryu-ji Raiyuki" states that it was founded by the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=King Man}} (King Mangō}} (first generation of It is said that it began when a descendant of the emperor, Yuzuki-kun's father) prayed to the ``God of the ancestors of the First Qin Emperor.''

Currently, it is enshrined as a small shrine next to the east of {{ill|Kōryū-ji|de|Kōryū-ji|fa|معبد کوریو|fr|Kōryū-ji|ja|広隆寺|ko|고류지|my|ခိုးရူးဂျိ|zh|廣隆寺|qid=Q3076920}}, but {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} Previously, it was a {{ill|Sangharama (Buddhist deity)|ja|伽藍神|th|พระสังฆารามโพธิสัตว์|zh|伽藍神|qid=Q10885799}} enshrined within the Katsuramiya-in of Koryu-ji Temple.

=== Outline ===
In {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi}}, {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}}2 years ({{ill|849|ab|849|af|849|als|849|am|849 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|849|ar|849|ary|849|arz|849|ast|849|avk|849|az|849|azb|۸۴۹ (میلادی)|bcl|849|be|849|be_x_old|849|bg|849|bn|৮৪৯|bpy|মারি ৮৪৯|br|849|bs|849.|ca|849|cdo|849 nièng|ceb|849|ckb|٨٤٩|crh|849|cs|849|csb|849|cv|849|cy|849|da|849|de|849|el|849|eml|849|eo|849|es|849|et|849|eu|849|fa|۸۴۹ (میلادی)|fi|849|fo|849|fr|849|frr|849|fy|849|ga|849|gan|849年|gd|849|gl|849|he|849|hi|849|hr|849.|ht|849 (almanak jilyen)|hu|849|hy|849|id|849|ilo|849|io|849|it|849|ja|849年|jv|849|ka|849|kaa|849|kk|849 жыл|ko|849년|la|849|lb|849|lij|849|lmo|849|lt|849 m.|lv|849. gads|map_bms|849|mdf|849|mg|849|mhr|849|mk|849|mr|इ.स. ८४९|mrj|849 и|ms|849|mzn|۸۴۹|nah|849|nap|849|nds|849|new|सन् ८४९|nl|849|nn|849|no|849|nrm|849|nso|849|oc|849|or|୮୪୯|os|849-æм аз|pl|849|pnb|849|pt|849|qu|849|ro|849|ru|849 год|rue|849|sa|८४९|scn|849|sd|849ع|se|849|sh|849.|shn|849|si|849|simple|849|sk|849|sl|849|smn|849|sq|849|sr|849|su|849|sv|849|sw|849|tg|Соли 849|th|พ.ศ. 1392|tk|849|tl|849|tly|849|tr|849|tt|849 ел|uk|849|ur|849ء|uz|849|vec|849|vi|849|war|849|wuu|849年|xmf|849|zh|849年|zh_min_nan|849 nî|zh_yue|849年|qid=Q23902}}) <ref group="Hara" In name="Kasho 2nd Year"/>, the ``Daisojin'' of {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276}}{{ill|Kadono district|Q13579879|qid=Q13579879}} has a miraculous experience. It is recorded that it was conferred the rank of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, which is lower than the Jugoi (Junior Fifth Rank) as a shrine {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} 5 years ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" It is listed in {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} as the original name of ``Osake-jinja Shrine (Shikiuchi-jinja)'', and it is also stated that it was originally the divine name of ``Osake-jinja Shrine (Shikiuchi-sha)|1979}}.In "Koryuji Raiyuki" <ref name="Raiyuki"/>, it is written that the shrine of ``Osake Daimyojin'' was promoted one after another, and in {{ill|Jiryaku|fa|جیریاکو|fr|Ère Jiryaku|ia|Jiryaku|id|Jiryaku|ja|治暦|ko|지랴쿠|ru|Дзиряку|simple|Jiryaku|sr|Џирјаку|tr|Jiryaku|zh|治曆|zh_yue|治曆|qid=Q934365}}4 year ({{ill|1068|Q19421|qid=Q19421}}) it reached the highest rank of Shoichii {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. Also, in the same article, it is said that it is one of the 38 shrines that were given to Koryuji during the {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} years ({{ill|901|Q23580|qid=Q23580}}-{{ill|923|Q30108|qid=Q30108}}) as one of the 38 shrines that were designated as shrines to Koryuji. {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1979}}.

{{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanbokucho period}} After the "Kuka Nikkoshu" in the Nanbokucho period}}, it appears in literature as the guardian shrine of Katsuragu-in of Koryu-ji Temple, and it moved along with Koryu-ji Temple {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was moved to its current location due to {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}. }, {{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}} was ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} in {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine rank system}}.

=== Setsusha ===
In the "Shikiuchi-sha Investigation Report", the following four shrines are listed as shrines within the precincts.
* Kogare Shrine
*: The enshrined deity is Okuninushi no Mikoto. "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan}} 4th year ({{ill|862|Q24993|qid=Q24993}}) Article <ref group =============================================================== </ref>{{Sfn|Kokare Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. “Koryuji Temple Raiyuki” <ref In name="Rayuki"/>, it appears as ``Kokare Myojin,'' and it is said that when the statue of {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|bg|Буда лечител|bn|ভৈষজ্যগুরু|bo|སྨན་བླ།|ca|Bhaishajyaguru|cs|Bhaišadžjaguru|de|Bhaisajyaguru|es|Bhaisajyaguru|fr|Bhaishajyaguru|hi|भैषज्यगुरु|hu|Bhaisadzsjaguru|id|Bhaiṣajyaguru|it|Bhaiṣajyaguru|ja|薬師如来|ko|약사여래|nl|Bhaisajyaguru|pl|Bhajszadźja|ro|Bhaisajyaguru|ru|Будда Медицины|si|භෛශජ්‍යගුරු බුදුන් වහන්සේ|sv|Bhaisajyaguru|ta|பைசையகுரு|te|భైషజ్యగురు బుద్ధుడు|th|พระไภษัชยคุรุ|tyv|Очуду|uk|Бгайсадж'я-гуру|ur|بھئشجیاگرو وئڈوریاپربھاراجہ|vi|Phật Dược Sư|wuu|药师佛|zh|藥師佛|qid=Q854773}} was brought to Koryuji Temple, Muko Myojin withered the Japanese japanese tree in front of the gate of Koryuji Temple, but when this deity was enshrined separately as ``Kokare Myojin,'' the tree was revived.{{Sfn|Kokare Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is not clear when it was moved to the current precincts of Taizaka Shrine, but it is presumed to have been moved after that time, as it appears in "Yamashiro Meishoshi" that it was enshrined in the rear garden of a private house south of the main gate of Koryuji Temple {{Sfn|Kokare Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.*: It is said that the shrine complex at the former enshrinement site of Kogarashi-jinja Shrine was called ``Kogara-no-mori'' (Kogara-no-mori). ``Kokare Mori'' is mentioned in ``Moriwa'' in the 194th paragraph of ``{{ill|The Pillow Book|Q615137|qid=Q615137}}'' and is also seen as ``{{ill|Utamakura|Q1588579|qid=Q1588579}}'' in ``{{ill|Gosen Wakashū|Q1538538|qid=Q1538538}}'', but these are compared to the Kogare Shrine in Yamashiro. === Festival ===
[[File:CowFesta.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|"{{ill|Miyako meisho zue|ja|都名所図会|qid=Q11643495}}" "Uzumasa Cow Festival Pictures"}}]]
One of the festivals at Osaka Shrine is known as the ``Ushimatsuri,'' which is held on the night of {{ill|October 12|Q2920|qid=Q2920}} (previously known as {{ill|September 12 (Lunisolar)|Q840306|qid=Q840306|lt=September 12th of the lunar calendar}}). {{ill|Chōwa|Q1194173|qid=Q1194173}} ({{ill|1012|Q19239|qid=Q19239}}-{{ill|1017|Q19249|qid=Q19249}}) (Monk)|Q1009263|Genshin}} (Eshin Sozu) is said to have started praying for {{ill|Matarajin|Q6380689|qid=Q6380689|lt=Matarajin}} as the guardian deity of Nembutsu, and during the period of syncretism of Shintoism and Buddhism, it was performed by the monks of Koryuji Temple. The Edo period festival is also depicted in ``{{ill|Miyako meisho zue|ja|都名所図会|qid=Q11643495}}''.During the festival, a person wearing a strange mask who plays the role of Matara-jin rides a bull and parades around the grounds of Koryu-ji Temple accompanied by the Four Heavenly Kings and a procession, and finally reads out the ritual in front of Yakushi-do Hall. This cow festival is counted as one of Kyoto's three strange festivals and is registered as a Kyoto City Registered Intangible Folk Cultural Property. Uzumasa Beef Festival] (Kyoto City homepage). </ref>{{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|Osake Shrine (Gods)|1986}} (Also see "{{ill|Kōryū-ji|de|Kōryū-ji|fa|معبد کوریو|fr|Kōryū-ji|ja|広隆寺|ko|고류지|my|ခိုးရူးဂျိ|zh|廣隆寺|qid=Q3076920}}").
